questions.question: When parking uphill on a road with no curb, set the parking brake and turn your wheels:

options.text: Toward the edge of the road.
Away from the edge of the road.
Straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Turn your front wheels toward the right edge of the road. If your brakes fail, your vehicle will roll away from the road instead of into it.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To better see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers often pass large vehicles from behind.
Because you will get caught in the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: To better see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: The driver of a large truck or bus may not see you directly behind them. Increase your distance so you can see the road ahead and around the sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: When roads are slippery after rain starts, you should:

options.text: Avoid making fast turns and stops.
Test your tires by driving uphill quickly.
Look less far ahead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making fast turns and stops.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire grip. Drive slowly and avoid sudden turns or stops to prevent skidding.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians still in the intersection.
Yield only to pedestrians in the intersection.
Wait four seconds before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians still in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. First, yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians in the intersection, then turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield sign ahead.
Side road entering from left.
Stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a yield sign is ahead. Start slowing down when you see this warning.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and watch for other drivers. Never change lanes or pass inside an intersection.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes lightly.
Stay off the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes during a skid. Keep steering until your vehicle is under control and moving safely.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, you should:

options.text: Touch one rear wheel to the curb.
Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park."
Keep your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park."
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and place the vehicle in "park" on a hill. If there is no curb, turn your wheels away from the center of the road so the vehicle rolls away if brakes fail.

questions.question: Large trucks are most likely to lose speed when:

options.text: Driving up long or steep hills.
Driving in long, gradual curves.
Driving down long, gradual hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take longer to speed up than smaller vehicles. They lose speed going uphill. Give trucks extra space, especially on hills.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
Assume the driver will let you pass if you signal.
Assume the driver will maintain constant speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even if you signal, do not assume other drivers will make space for you or give you the right-of-way.

questions.question: When exiting the interstate, when should you start slowing down?

options.text: Halfway through the deceleration lane.
As you approach the deceleration lane.
Right when you enter the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Keep your speed the same until you enter the deceleration lane. Then slow down to match the posted advisory speed for the exit ramp.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow light at an intersection. You have not entered it yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass through before the red light.
Slow down and carefully drive through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a steady yellow light and have not entered the intersection, stop safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Let all traffic pass before you cross.
Stop, then cross when it is safe.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down to a safe speed and proceed with caution through the intersection.

questions.question: How should you avoid glare from an oncoming car's headlights?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Keep your eyes on the centerline of the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Do not look at the bright lights of an oncoming vehicle. Instead, glance briefly toward the right side of the road. Then look ahead again to track the other vehicle's position.

questions.question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find another route.
Go to the next exit, leave the freeway, and find your proper exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up on the road or shoulder. Continue to the next exit instead. Other drivers will not expect a car backing up and a collision is likely.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, how fast should you be driving?

options.text: At about the same speed as traffic on the freeway.
Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
The posted speed limit for the freeway.

questions.correctAnswerText: At about the same speed as traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: Merge onto the freeway at or near the speed of traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: What do broken yellow lines on roads and highways mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
They separate lanes moving in the same direction.
They separate lanes moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: They separate lanes moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken lines mean passing is allowed when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road will get narrower ahead.
There are curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They alert you to road conditions ahead. This sign warns you about a winding road with curves.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Press the brake pedal hard.
Hold the wheel tight and use light brake pressure.
Pull over right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the wheel tight and use light brake pressure.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas and using light braking. Pull off the road in a safe place when you can.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge to the right.
A divided highway is starting.
The right lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the right lane is ending ahead. Drivers in that lane will need to merge into another lane.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels left to prepare for the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Always signal about 100 feet before turning. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another car hits you from behind.

questions.question: You and the driver on your left reach a four-way stop at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left has the right-of-way.
You have the right-of-way.
Whoever is signaling to turn has the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the car ahead?

options.text: When you are following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, create extra space ahead. Slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid a crash with the tailgater.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the road ahead is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline means you can cross it to pass another vehicle on the left if there is no oncoming traffic. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.

questions.question: What must you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
Slow down and continue with caution.
Stop completely and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely. Then proceed when it is safe.
